Factory:
Factory is a location in Escape from Tarkov. It is the first map that was added to the game.


Description
The industrial estate and facilities of Chemical Plant No. 16 were rented out illegally to the TerraGroup corporation. During the advent of the Contract Wars, the plant became the scene of numerous firefights between BEAR and USEC that ultimately determined control over the industrial district of Tarkov. Later on, in the wake of the chaos, the plant facilities became a shelter for the remaining civilians, Scavs, and military operatives, including the scattered remains of the BEAR and USEC contingents.


Notes
Factory is initially only accessible by transiting. Direct access from the location selection screen is unlocked upon progressing through the story chapter Tour.

Shoreline:
Shoreline is a location in Escape from Tarkov. It is the fourth map that was added to the game.


Description
The Shoreline area makes up a large part of the outskirts of Tarkov and is located next to the Port. The area houses a partially abandoned village, modern private housing, agricultural fields, long stretches of beach, a boating facility, gas station, weather station, and a cellular tower as well as other commercial facilities. Shoreline's main point of interest is the Azure Coast health resort which consists of several blocks, exclusively powered by a nearby hydroelectric power plant. The resort had previously been used as temporary accommodation for members of TerraGroup and the corporation's associated divisions in preparation for the evacuation of the Tarkov Port.


Notes
Shoreline is initially only accessible by transiting. Direct access from the location selection screen is unlocked upon progressing through the story chapter Tour.


Features
Stationary weapons in the form of AGS-30 30x29mm automatic grenade launchers and NSV Utyos 12.7x108 heavy machine guns.
Be aware of Border Snipers and Minefields!


Port Terminal
The Terminal is guarded by RUAF soldiers and machine gunners. They are neutral towards the player but will open fire when they get shot, and if a player gets too close to the Terminal without presenting an access item at the port garrison intercom. Check our maps to keep a safe distance.

Lighthouse:
Lighthouse is a location in Escape from Tarkov. It is the eighth map that was added to the game.


Description
The lighthouse at Cape Dalniy was an important strategic object on the way to Tarkov. During Contract Wars, it was the main entry point for USEC units and served as their base of operations. Features
Be aware of Minefields, Claymores and Border Snipers!


Lighthouse
The lighthouse at the peninsula territory is the home of Lightkeeper. The bridge that leads to the lighthouse is guarded by Zryachiy and full of Claymores. To safely pass the bridge, an encoded Digital secure DSP radio transmitter is required. It deactivates the claymores and has Zryachiy not shoot you. The questline to obtain one starts with To the Light - Trust but Verify. Harming Zryachiy, one of his followers, or a Lightkeeper acquainted PMC in the lighthouse premises will decode your Digital secure DSP radio transmitter if you have one. PMCs that are acquainted with Lightkeeper can kill unacquainted intruders without penalty.

The Labyrinth, also known as "Labrys", is a location in Escape from Tarkov. It is the eleventh map that was added to the game. 


Description

Features


Insurance
All insured items left in a raid by players will not be returned. Upon death, insurance Traders will send the usual in-game mail about dispatching people to recover the items, but when the insurance timer runs out they will explain that their people don't go to the location, didn't find it or died in the process.


Spawn chambers
Each of the 5 spawns has its entry to the rest of the location blocked by a hazard/trap, which needs to be resolved to not die.


Chamber 1 - Toxic pool

1. Find Key 01
2. Unlock the door in the left side room
3. Press the button on the wall


Chamber 2 - Steam hazard

1. Find Key 02
2. Unlock the red door
3. Find the Valve handwheel on the 2nd floor
4. Apply the handwheel to the pipe next to the yellow door on the 1st floor


Chamber 3 - Fire hazard

1. Find Key 03
2. Unlock the far door
3. Find the BBQ-S43 gas torch
4. Apply the gas torch to the door at the start
5. Press the button at the electrical cabinet


Chamber 4 - Shotgun trap

1. Find Key 04
2. Unlock the 2nd door
3. Crawl into the connected room
4. Pull the lever to the left of the door
5. Breach the door


Chamber 5 - Toxic puddle

1. Find the BBQ-S43 gas torch
2. Apply the gas torch to the round door in the left side room
3. Pull the lever on the wall

The barbed wire has set locations, but it is random in which it appears every raid. Upon contact, there is a chance to get inflicted with the  effect, which deals gradual damage over time (140 HP/minute). It can be treated with an xTG-12 or Perfotoran injector.

In Escape from Tarkov, transits are used for map to map travel without leaving a raid.
Transits are available 1 minute after the start of a raid and have a 20 second timer. Once a transit has been activated, extractions can no longer be used. All players of a lobby-made group need to be in the transit area for a transition to succeed, otherwise the timer restarts.

Item delivery
When using a transit as PMC, players can send items to their stash for a fee. Items will arrive after 1 hour via the mail system.
The size of the delivery inventory is influenced by your Scav karma.

Boss:
Bosses are powerful enemies with unique gear, traits and behavior in Escape from Tarkov.


Event bosses
Map_of_Tarkov:
The map in Escape from Tarkov consists of 13 different locations. While they are separated from each other, it is possible to transit between them without leaving a round.


Location selection
Most maps are initially locked in the location selection and get unlocked by progressing through the story chapter Tour. A red skull icon  indicates the guaranteed presence of a boss at that location.


Location specific features


Minefields

Minefields are usually marked by warning signs, but there are also a few unmarked ones (e.g. west of the USEC camp on Woods).The mines are invisible, respawn after they detonate and can only be triggered by players. It is therefore impossible to detect a mine, let alone clear a minefield. When entering a minefield, triggering a mine is chance-based.While they are used to create artificial borders on Woods, Shoreline, Ground Zero, Interchange and Reserve, they can also be found along the harbor terminal wall on Shoreline.


Border Snipers

Border Snipers are marked by various warning signs. They are invisible, non-killable and can shoot through any object. They should be avoided under all circumstances, not least because the player's health will be set to 1% after dying to them.It is therefore essential for survival to retreat immediately when being targeted by one, as taking cover is pointless.They are used to create artificial borders on Customs, Lighthouse, Reserve, Woods, Shoreline, Ground Zero, Interchange and Streets of Tarkov.


Claymores

Claymores are directional anti-personnel mines. The mines have an activation range of 5-10m, are unaffected by gunfire and explosives and instantly kill players upon detonation, unless they are behind cover. Unlike the minefield, once blown up another doesn't respawn in its place, allowing claymores to be permanently cleared after detonation. Claymores can only be detonated by getting into their activation range.
They are used on the Lighthouse, Ground Zero and Streets of Tarkov locations:

On Lighthouse they are scattered on the bridge to the lighthouse at the peninsula territory. It is possible to safely pass them with an encoded Digital secure DSP radio transmitter.
On Ground Zero one is located inside the Tarbank, in customer desk booth no. 3.
On Streets of Tarkov they are scattered around the LexOs car dealership.
